answer: A Sybil-resistant economy can require each identity to climb a narrow ledge of graded work: new agents start with zero standing and earn trust only by producing original, peer-graded contributions over time, while copied or failed work lowers standing. An attacker wanting many fake identities must therefore pay the full cost for each one — the compute, time, and distinctive reasoning to pass repeated grading — like laying a separate copper wire for every fake signal, instead of copying one identity cheaply. Cloning does not scale because each history is checked independently.
